findings.claim: The new `MarkOptions.kind` is typed as the full `BrowserTraceEntryKind` union, allowing callers to emit `'action'`, `'expect'`, or `'lifecycle'` entries through the public mark API
findings.rationale: `'action'`, `'expect'` and `'lifecycle'` look like kinds the runtime itself produces for locator actions, assertions and test lifecycle boundaries. Exposing them on a user-facing `mark()` option lets user code inject entries that the trace viewer (and any logic that pairs lifecycle start/end entries) treats as engine-generated, which can corrupt the rendered trace. The documented default `'mark'` suggests a marker-only subset was intended. Medium confidence — depends on how the consumer of `kind` interprets the values, which is not visible in this hunk.

findings.claim: `stack?: string` is an untyped free-form string with no documented format or defined failure behavior when it cannot be parsed
findings.rationale: Stack parsing is environment-dependent (V8 vs Firefox/Safari formats). Accepting an arbitrary string means a wrapper library passing a non-V8 or truncated stack will silently produce a wrong or missing marker location, or potentially throw during parsing. Worth confirming the consumer falls back to a captured stack rather than emitting a bogus file/line. Low-to-medium confidence since the parsing code is not in this hunk.

findings.claim: `MarkOptions` is a very generic name newly added to the public `vitest/browser` type surface
findings.rationale: As a newly exported public symbol, a generic name like `MarkOptions` can collide with declarations from other packages in consumers' ambient/merged type space and is ambiguous next to the more specific sibling `BrowserTraceEntryKind`. `BrowserMarkOptions` would be consistent and reduce collision risk. This affects the published API shape, though practical impact is low.
